oil.summary: Crude sold off sharply on the day despite a geopolitically charged backdrop: WTI fell 2.33% to $71.81 and Brent dropped 2.54% to $76.04, though both benchmarks remain well bid on a weekly basis (+4.71% and +6.25% respectively) following last week's risk premium build. The steepest move was in RBOB gasoline, off 8.16% to $2.8501, suggesting demand-side pressure is overwhelming supply fears for now. The news flow is intensely bullish on paper — Ukraine struck 8 Russian shadow-fleet tankers in the Sea of Azov, hit oil depots in Stavropol and Tver, and Russia has banned diesel exports citing refinery damage. Separately, the US revoked Iran's sanctions waiver after tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and launched retaliatory strikes on Iranian targets. Indonesia took delivery of its first Russian crude under the April deal, illustrating continued rerouting of sanctioned barrels. The monthly loss of over 19-21% signals the market is pricing demand weakness above geopolitical risk.
drivers: Ukraine drone campaign escalating against Russian shadow fleet and refinery infrastructure, Russia bans diesel exports in response
US revokes Iran sanctions waiver and launches strikes after Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks, tightening Iranian supply outlook
RBOB gasoline -8.16% on the day signals demand-side deterioration overwhelming geopolitical risk premium; WTI -21% over 30 days reflects macro bear trend

gas.summary: A sharp divergence between Henry Hub and TTF defined the session. Henry Hub fell 6.23% to $3.012/MMBtu, extending a weekly loss of 6.46% and pointing to ample domestic supply conditions in the US. TTF moved in the opposite direction, gaining 2.04% to €50.02/MWh and surging 16.93% on the week, driven by Hormuz disruption anxiety. Pakistan was forced into the spot LNG market after a Qatari cargo was cancelled, a direct consequence of Strait of Hormuz re-escalation — a concrete demand signal for spot cargoes. The European Commission is set to announce a 2040 electrification target next week, a medium-term bearish structural signal for gas, though it offers no near-term relief to the TTF spike.
drivers: Pakistan forced into emergency spot LNG buying after Qatar cargo cancellation tied to Strait of Hormuz disruption, tightening spot market
TTF surges 16.93% on the week as European buyers price in Hormuz and Russian supply risk simultaneously
Henry Hub -6.23% on the day and -6.46% on the week, reflecting US-specific supply sufficiency decoupled from global geopolitical tensions

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs were broadly flat on the day, slipping just 0.08% to $74.725/EUA, with the monthly gain of 2.08% intact. The key market mover for the power complex remains TTF, up 2.04% on the day and 16.93% on the week, which raises gas-fired generation costs across Europe. On the structural side, the European Commission is expected to unveil a 2040 electrification target next week aimed at reducing fossil fuel dependence and expanding renewables — a long-run EUA demand dampener if successful. A US firm advancing thorium molten-salt reactor development and the shipping industry's retreat from green fuels due to cost pressures are noteworthy longer-dated signals, though neither moves markets today. Overall, the power and carbon sector has limited fresh price catalysts today; geopolitical spillovers from oil and gas dominate the macro backdrop.
drivers: TTF +16.93% on the week raises gas-fired power generation costs across Europe, pressuring power margins
European Commission set to reveal 2040 electrification target next week, a structural medium-term signal for reduced fossil fuel demand
EUA prices near flat on the day; near-term carbon price direction remains hostage to TTF and broader macro sentiment rather than policy catalysts
